Self-checks and test signals¶

Test recording¶

iqgen writes a 2 s capture at 2 MS/s:

./build/iqgen out.sigmf-data --fmt ci16

The capture contains these signals:

Offset

Signal

+300 kHz

FM, 1 kHz tone, 50 kHz deviation, slow fade

−250 kHz

AM, 400 Hz tone, 60 % depth

−600 kHz

PM, 2 rad sine, plus 90° steps each 20 ms

+650 kHz

2-FSK bursts

+100 kHz

A weak CW tone

—

A chirp from 1.0 s to 1.4 s

To examine the FM signal, type wvt out.sigmf-meta --chan 300k:150k --view 0.5:0.505.

The sim device streams synthetic signals without hardware: wvt --device sim -c 100M -r 2.4M.

Self-check programs¶

The self-checks do not need hardware. Each program shows its result and returns a non-zero exit code if a check fails.

Program

Checks

build/siggen_check

The signal generator: waveforms, sweeps, chains, playback cache, chain files and the file output

build/audio_check

Each audio demodulator mode

build/log_check

The logger: levels, options, the log file and threads

build/segment_check

The time segment rules and the overview on a sample range

build/extract_check

The region export: copies, the band filter, metadata, input checks and cancel

build/snapshot_check

Plot snapshots: file names, numbering, the crop and the PNG files

build/session_check

File sessions: write and read back, the recording after a folder move, session files and recordings told apart, no replace without asking, bad values

build/measure_check

Point measurements: the nearest sample, the snap to a peak or a valley, which differences apply, the plot names

build/device_check

The device list entries from a UHD search, device arguments and the sample rate rules

build/clipboard_check

The system clipboard, both ways, with a second X client: UTF-8, Latin-1, large texts in parts. It needs an X server (for example xvfb-run -a build/clipboard_check); without one it is skipped

build/bb_check

The BB60 backend with the simulated device: open, rates, bandwidths, streaming, overload, unplug, and the capture segments of a recording across retunes. Only with -DWVT_BB_SIM=ON

build/skiq_check

The Sidekiq logic: the gain in dB to a gain index, the lost samples from the RF timestamps, the 12-bit scaling and the I/Q order. With -DWVT_SKIQ_SIM=ON, also the backend with the simulated card: open and its errors, streaming, the tone level on a 12-bit and a 16-bit card, a retune while streaming, overload, USB, an overrun and a card removal

build/gpu_check

The GPU results against the CPU results. --bench measures the speed

To run all of them, use CTest:

ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure

CTest shows each program as one test. To run one program, add -R NAME, for example -R extract_check.

Sanitizer builds¶

wvt has many threads, lock-free rings and memory-mapped files. Run the self-checks in a sanitizer build to find memory errors and data races. Refer to WVT_SANITIZE.

cmake -S . -B build-asan -DWVT_SANITIZE=address -DWVT_BB_SIM=ON
cmake --build build-asan -j
cmake -S . -B build-tsan -DWVT_SANITIZE=thread -DWVT_BB_SIM=ON
cmake --build build-tsan -j

Then run the self-checks from build-asan/ and build-tsan/. A sanitizer error stops the program with a report and a non-zero exit code.

Note

On Linux kernels with a high address-space randomization (for example Ubuntu 24.04), ThreadSanitizer can stop with unexpected memory mapping. Then type sudo sysctl vm.mmap_rnd_bits=28 before you run the checks.

Fuzz tests¶

The fuzz targets give random and mutated input to the parsers that read text from files and from the user. They need clang with libFuzzer (on macOS: the Homebrew llvm, because Apple clang has no libFuzzer). Refer to WVT_FUZZ.

Program

Parser

fuzz_json

parseJson and the typed getters of JsonValue

fuzz_chain

loadChain (chain files), then checkParams on the result

fuzz_meta

guessMeta: file names (gqrx and the rate and frequency in a name) and SigMF metadata files

fuzz_parse_si

parseSI, the number parser of the command line and the input fields (2.4M, 915 MHz)

To build them and run them on their seed inputs (tools/fuzz/corpus/):

cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DWVT_FUZZ=ON -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++
cmake --build build-fuzz -j --target fuzz_json fuzz_chain fuzz_meta fuzz_parse_si
ctest --test-dir build-fuzz -R '^fuzz_' --output-on-failure

To fuzz one parser for 10 minutes, use a copy of the seed inputs. libFuzzer adds new inputs to the first folder that you give it, and you do not want them in the repository:

cp -r tools/fuzz/corpus/chain /tmp/corpus-chain
./build-fuzz/fuzz_chain -max_total_time=600 -max_len=4096 /tmp/corpus-chain

If the program finds a problem, it stops with a report and writes the input to a crash-... file. To run that input again, type ./build-fuzz/fuzz_chain crash-....

Static analysis¶

clang-tidy checks the wvt code with the bugprone, cert, concurrency and performance check families. The configuration is in .clang-tidy. It turns off the checks that found only intended code in wvt, and gives the reason for each. tools/.clang-tidy turns off some more checks for the test programs. A finding is an error. To run it as CI does:

cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON
pip install clang-tidy==23.1.3
tools/run-clang-tidy.sh build

Use the same clang-tidy version as CI, because a different version can find different things. To accept one finding on purpose, put // NOLINT(check-name) and the reason on the line.

Continuous integration¶

GitHub Actions builds each pull request and each push to main (.github/workflows/build.yml):

Job

Contents

Linux (CPU, RTL-SDR, UHD)

Builds with the two device backends and the simulated BB60, runs all self-checks with CTest and some command-line runs

macOS (Apple silicon, Metal, RTL-SDR, UHD)

Builds on an Apple silicon runner with XQuartz, Accelerate, the Metal backend, the two device backends and the simulated BB60. Runs all self-checks and the same command-line runs as the Linux job

Linux CUDA 12.0 and 12.8

Builds the CUDA backend. The runners have no GPU, so the job makes sure that a CUDA build runs on the CPU

Sanitizers (address, thread)

Builds with WVT_SANITIZE=address (ASan and UBSan) and with WVT_SANITIZE=thread (TSan), and runs all self-checks

clang-tidy

Runs tools/run-clang-tidy.sh (clang-tidy 23.1.3). A finding causes the job to fail

Fuzz the parsers

Builds the fuzz targets with clang, runs them on the seed inputs, then fuzzes each one for 60 s. If a fuzz target finds a problem, the job keeps the input as a fuzz-crashes artifact

Documentation

Builds these pages with Sphinx. A warning causes the job to fail

The Linux, macOS and CUDA build jobs use WVT_WERROR=ON: a compiler warning in the wvt code causes the job to fail.
